newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-DJORKAEFF SPOILS RUSSIA'S CENTENARY PARTY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DJORKAEFF SPOILS RUSSIA'S CENTENARY PARTY.

text.p: Inter Milan's French striker Youri Djorkaeff helped Bobby Robson's World XI beat a ragged-looking Russia 2-0 on Monday in a match celebrating the country's soccer centenary.
In a game with few real chances, Djorkaeff pounced when Russian goalkeeper Stanislav Cherchesov had a free kick awarded against him for illegally handling the ball.

The Frenchman blasted the lay-off into the roof of the net in the 52nd minute. Atletico Madrid's Julen Guerrero made it two 12 minutes from time, turning in a cross from Germany's Stefan Effenberg who rounded Cherchesov on the edge of the box.
Some 55,000 fans, including President Boris Yeltsin, packed the newly refurbished Luzhniki stadium -- the biggest crowd Russian football has seen in years.
Now roofed over at a cost of $200 million and seating 82,000 when all the stands are open, the stadium is in line to host a European club final next year.
The home side, even after eight substitutions at half-time, gave the crowd little cheer in marking a century since the first Russian sides played competitive soccer.
The players were booed off by some of the crowd.

Coach Boris Ignatyev, who takes his squad to St Petersburg on Wednesday for a friendly against Yugoslavia, knows they must improve if they are to overcome Bulgaria in a pair of crucial World Cup qualifying fixtures over the next two months.
Only 13 foreigners turned up out of a couple of dozen international stars originally invited by former England manager Robson, forcing him to draft in some Russian stand-ins.
But the World XI, captained by Bayern Munich's Lothar Matthaeus, played with more cohesion than the hosts.
Bordeaux's Jean-Pierre Papin, Inter's Dutch midfielder Aron Winter, Abedi Pele of Ghana and 1860 Munich, as well as Borussia Moenchengladbach's Effenberg, all had chances.
